{{one source |date=May 2024}}
A '''geodesic circle''' is either "the [[locus (mathematics)|locus]] on a [[surface (mathematics)|surface]] at a constant [[geodesic]] [[distance]] from a fixed [[point (geometry)|point]]" or a [[curve]] of constant [[geodesic curvature]].<ref name="Whittemore1901">{{cite journal | last=Whittemore | first=J. K. | title=A Note on Geodesic Circles | journal=The Annals of Mathematics |jstor=1967629 | volume=3 | issue=1/4 | year=1901 | pages=21–24 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.2307/1967629 }}</ref> 
A '''geodesic disk''' is the region on a surface bounded by a geodesic circle.
In contrast with the ordinary [[circle]] and [[disk (mathematics)|disk]], the geodesic circle is not necessarily a [[plane curve]] and the geodesic disk is not necessarily a [[planar surface]].
They can be used to define ''[[Gaussian_curvature#Alternative_formulas|Gaussian curvature]]''.
